title: Halasana

sequence.action: Arms up, palms together, gaze at the fingertips
Fold forward, hands beside the feet, nose to the knees
Lie down, arms by the sides, legs straight; puraka and rechaka four to five times
Join together and raise the legs, as in Sarvangasana.

Slowly lower the legs to the floor over the head, keeping them straight, place the feet on the floor, lock the fingers behind the back, arms tight and straight, press the chin into the chest without bending the legs, and do puraka and rechaka deeply, as much as possible.
Hands beside the head, roll back over the head into Chaturanga Dandasana
Jump the feet between the hands, lift the head

while_holding: Both rechaka and puraka occur in the 8th vinyasa.
benefits: Halasana purifies the intestines, the region of the waist, and the throat channel, and strengthens them.

By means of these five asanas, the vishuddhi chakra [throat chakra], heart, lungs, limbs, digestive system, and jathara [stomach] are purified, and perversions of the vital wind, which result in hiccups, dry cough, constipation, and indigestion, as well as high blood pressure, are warded off.
They also prevent illnesses such as asthma, and ailments related to the heart.
benefits_source: Given in the book under Pindasana, as the benefits of asanas 32 to 36; the last two apply to all five.
